notes.text: aⁿbⁿ ↦ bⁿaⁿ. The stack does the counting that makes aⁿbⁿ context-free: one X pushed per a, one popped per b, and the final ε-move only succeeds when Z is back on top — i.e. when the counts matched. The output swaps the letters as it goes.

Two jobs at once: the stack decides membership in a context-free language while the output function computes a transduction over the accepting runs. Try aab (unbalanced) — the run cannot reach "balanced", so the pair is not in the relation and nothing is output.

meta.title: Classic: aⁿbⁿ ↦ bⁿaⁿ
meta.blurb: Accepts aⁿbⁿ with the stack while printing b for every a and a for every b — so the output is bⁿaⁿ. Recognition and transduction in one machine.
